A warm welcome to
Aragon Primary School
Welcome to Aragon Primary School's website! We are thrilled to have you here and excited to share with you all the wonderful things that our school has to offer.
Aragon is a happy, ambitious and inclusive school where children are encouraged to “Be the best we can be.” This isn’t just a motto for us – it’s something we live and breathe every day. We want every child to do well, but just as importantly, to feel confident in who they are and secure in what they can achieve. Success looks different for every child, and we celebrate that.
When people visit Aragon, they often tell us they can feel the warmth of the school straight away. They notice the smiles, the calm atmosphere, the excellent behaviour, and the way children and staff treat each other with respect and kindness. There is a real sense of belonging here, and a shared belief that every child matters.
We are very proud of our children’s achievements. Outcomes are consistently strong from the Early Years through to Year 6. In 2025, our Key Stage 2 attainment was the fourth highest in the London Borough of Merton, with pupils achieving significantly above national averages over several years.
Our May 2025 Ofsted inspection recognised the school’s significant improvement, highlighting our pupils’ exemplary behaviour, strong curriculum and teaching, and caring, purposeful learning environment. These achievements reflect the hard work of our children and staff, as well as the support and partnership of our families.
An Aragon education is about much more than academic success. We want children to experience joy, challenge, friendship, creativity, sport, music and play. We encourage them to discover their interests, develop their confidence and build an understanding of the wider world.
Whether you are already part of our community or considering joining us, we hope our website gives you a sense of what makes Aragon special. We would love you to come and see our school for yourself, meet our children and staff, and experience the warm and welcoming atmosphere we are so proud of.
Please contact the school office, email aragon@aragon.merton.sch.uk or book a tour. We would be delighted to welcome you.
Our Latest Social Media
Our School Council had an unforgettable visit to the Houses of Parliament, where we were warmly welcomed by our local MP, Siobhain McDonagh. From exploring one of the UK's most iconic buildings to learning about democracy in action, the children were inspired every step of the way. They asked thoughtful questions, represented our school brilliantly and even held their final School Council meeting of the year in an official Parliamentary meeting room! A huge thank you to Siobhain for sharing her time, knowledge and passion with us. It was a fascinating experience and a day our pupils will remember for years to come. #SchoolCouncil #HousesOfParliament #PupilVoice #DemocracyInAction #FutureLeaders #PrimarySchoolLife #LearningBeyondTheClassroom #MertonSchools #ParliamentVisit
What a wonderful way to celebrate the diversity of our school community! Last Friday, pupils proudly wore clothing representing their own countries, cultures and family heritage as part of our Languages Week celebrations. It was fantastic to see so many nationalities represented and to celebrate the rich mix of backgrounds that make Aragon such a vibrant and inclusive school. #LanguagesWeek #Diversity #Inclusion #ProudToBeAragon #CelebratingCulture #BelongingAtAragon
Healthy Me Week is coming! From Monday 29th June to Friday 3rd July, we'll be celebrating with our theme Ignite Your Spark! Across the week, children will take part in a range of new sports and activities, enjoy visits from external providers and take part in their Sports Day. Highlights include a whole-school House Sports Afternoon and a special street dance assembly. Children can wear their sports kit all week please ensure full Aragon PE kit is worn on their Sports Day (and ideally on Monday too). We're looking forward to a brilliant week!

Curriculum Vision
"The school has carefully planned what pupils learn at each stage of the curriculum, and this is set out so that pupils build on what they already know. The curriculum is delivered expertly. Teaching is underpinned by strong subject knowledge. Teachers use effective models to support pupils’ understanding. They check pupils’ knowledge and intervene promptly when misconceptions arise. Pupils have plenty of opportunities to practise and consolidate their learning. As a result, pupils remember key concepts and can apply them across different areas of the curriculum. Teachers quickly and effectively spot any special educational needs and/or disabilities. They use their careful assessments to provide highly effective adaptations so that pupils can learn the curriculum well." Ofsted May 2025

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
It is a real privilege to welcome you to Aragon Primary School.
Aragon is a happy, ambitious and inclusive school where children are encouraged to “Be the best we can be.” This isn’t just a motto for us – it’s something we live and breathe every day. We want every child to do well, but just as importantly, to feel confident in who they are and secure in what they can achieve. Success looks different for every child, and we celebrate that.
When people visit Aragon, they often tell us they can feel the warmth of the school straight away. They notice the smiles, the calm atmosphere, the excellent behaviour, and the way children and staff treat each other with respect and kindness. There is a real sense of belonging here, and a shared belief that every child matters.
We believe that a great primary education should be both challenging and joyful. Our children benefit from high-quality teaching, a carefully planned and ambitious curriculum, and a wide range of experiences that bring learning to life. These include clubs, sport, music, trips, visitors and hands-on opportunities that help children discover new interests and talents. We are also thrilled to be an OPAL Platinum School, placing us in the top 2% nationally for the quality of our play provision. Play is a vital part of childhood, and we are committed to making it rich, inclusive and full of imagination.
We are very proud of our pupils’ achievements. Outcomes are consistently strong from the Early Years through to Year 6, and our children regularly achieve above national averages. But for us, education is about much more than results. We want children to leave Aragon with confidence, curiosity, resilience and a strong sense of who they are.
Our values of ambition, belonging, curiosity, kindness and responsibility run through everything we do. We have high expectations of both learning and behaviour because we believe every child deserves to learn in a calm, safe and respectful environment. We are also deeply inclusive and work hard to ensure that every child is supported, included and able to succeed in their own way.
If you are considering Aragon for your child, I hope our website gives you a genuine sense of what we are about. We know that choosing a school is a hugely important decision, and we never take the trust families place in us for granted. We work closely with parents and carers so that every child is known well, supported carefully and able to flourish from the very start of their journey with us.
Of course, a website can only say so much. The best way to understand Aragon is to come and see it for yourself – to meet our children and staff, and to feel the energy and warmth of the school in person. We would be delighted to welcome you for a visit.
I feel incredibly proud to be Headteacher of Aragon Primary School, and excited about everything children, families and staff can achieve together.
Adam Gilbert Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Working in Partnership
At Aragon Primary School, we believe that working in partnership with other schools, educational institutions, and community providers is vital. These collaborations enrich our curriculum, enhance professional development for our staff, and ultimately support the best possible outcomes for our pupils. By working together, we share expertise, strengthen teaching practices, and create meaningful learning experiences. Our partnerships also benefit the organisations we collaborate with, providing them with opportunities to work in and with an innovative and high-quality educational setting.
Our Key Partnerships
The Willow Learning Trust As a proud member of The Willow Learning Trust, we work closely with both Abbey Primary School and Glenthorne High School. Our collaboration with Abbey Primary allows subject leaders to strengthen their curriculum areas and year groups to co-develop outstanding lessons. We also participate in cross-school moderation to maintain high standards. At Glenthorne High School, we benefit from specialist teaching, particularly in Modern Foreign Languages (MFL), which enhances our curriculum provision.
Sean McInnes Sports Coaching (SMSC) SMSC is based at our school and provides high-quality PE coaching, ensuring our pupils engage in dynamic and stimulating physical education. Their coaches also enhance our lunchtime provision, promoting active and structured play opportunities for all children.
Merton Schools Sports Partnership (MSSP) Through MSSP, we access expert PE coaching and specialist CPD for our staff. This ensures our teachers continually develop their skills, leading to high-quality PE lessons for our pupils.
Merton Special Training Association (MSTA) MSTA delivers part of their training courses at Aragon Primary School. Trainee teachers and professionals from local schools visit us to observe our high-quality teaching and learn from our best practice.
Teacher Training – Sutton SCITT Aragon Primary School is a hub for Initial Teacher Training (ITT) through Sutton SCITT. Our trainee teachers gain hands-on experience in our classrooms, learning from our expert practitioners.
Teacher Training – Roehampton University We work closely with Roehampton University, regularly hosting their trainee teachers, who benefit from our high standards of teaching and mentoring.
NESCOT College Students from NESCOT College complete placements in our Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) setting, learning from our outstanding practitioners and gaining essential hands-on experience in early childhood education.
Wandle Teaching School We serve as a hub for Merton’s Early Career Teachers (ECTs), who attend regular training sessions led by Mr Gilbert. These sessions provide vital professional development to support the next generation of teachers. Additionally, Miss Pearce works with the Wandle Teaching School as a Literacy Specialist, providing support to local schools in developing their phonics provision.
Outdoor Play and Learning (OPAL) Our partnership with OPAL ensures that our lunchtime provision is engaging and enriching for all pupils. Working closely with OPAL mentors, we continuously develop and enhance our outdoor play opportunities.
Merton Local Authority While we are part of The Willow Learning Trust, we remain actively engaged with Merton Local Authority. We participate in their training programmes and frequently serve as a host school for borough-wide professional development sessions, supporting the wider educational community.
King’s College Wimbledon Through their outreach programme, our Year 5 children regularly attend gifted and talented enrichment sessions in maths, drama, and performance. We also participate in their Connect Programme, which supports pupil premium children in gaining access to schools requiring entrance exams.
Raynes Park High School (RPHS) We work closely with RPHS, regularly visiting their school to participate in various learning experiences and use their excellent facilities. Our children benefit from DT workshops, cooking and nutrition sessions, sports activities, and STEM-focused learning.
Wimbledon Dons We actively support the Wimbledon Dons food bank, collecting food donations to help those in need. This initiative began during lockdown and has continued to grow, strengthening our community links and instilling a sense of social responsibility in our pupils.
Local Religious Links We work closely with local religious communities, including Emmanuel Church, St Martin’s Church, The Baitul Futuh Mosque, and Morden Park Baptist Church. Our children regularly visit these religious sites for events such as carol concerts and enriching, interactive events such as 'The Christmas Journey', as well as to deepen their understanding of Christianity and Islam. Rev. Ken Franklin and Vicar David Ruddick also deliver regular assemblies, further enriching our pupils' spiritual and cultural education.
By fostering these valuable partnerships, we enhance the educational experience of our pupils, provide exceptional professional development for our staff, and contribute to the broader educational landscape. Together, we are stronger, and our collective efforts ensure that Aragon Primary School continues to thrive as a centre of excellence in education.

Curriculum Overview​​​​​​​
The Early Years Foundation Stage is based around four themes:
Each theme is linked to an important principle.
Every child is a competent learner from birth who can be resilient, capable, confident and self-assured.
Children learn to be strong and independent from a base of loving and secure relationships with parents and/or a key person.
The environment plays a key role in supporting and extending children's development and learning.
Children develop and learn in different ways and at different rates and all areas of learning and development are equally important and interconnected.
There are seven areas of learning and development that shape educational programmes in Early Years settings. All areas of learning and development are important and inter-connected.
We use these seven areas of learning as a framework to plan our curriculum in Nursery and Reception.
As of September 2021, we implemented this brand new Phonics Scheme of Work here at Aragon. We have been amazed by the positive impact it has had on our Early Reading skills and we are delighted to be continuing to follow it next year. You can take a look at the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds website parents page for a sneaky look at what your child will be doing in their phonics sessions.

Here at Aragon we have been following the Maths No Problem Scheme of Work for a number of years successfully. As of September 2021, a Maths No Problem Early Years Scheme of Work was released and we are very excited to be following it. Maths No Problem uses a spiral approach to ensure depth of learning and a secure understanding of key mathematical concepts.

Nursery
Nursery Information
Welcome to Nursery
This is Nursery's information page where you can find all relevant information regarding your child's class and daily routines.
Nursery's support staff are:
Please see the school website to ensure you have the full school uniform.
Please remember to label all items of clothing with your child's name clearly.
All Aragon Primary logo items are available from Your School Uniform - delivery is free if sent via school.
On a Tuesday, Nursery will be having their PE session. Therefore, they can come into school wearing their school PE kits on this day. During winter months, please ensure your child also has their school jumper.
The school P.E kit worn should be as follows: their house-coloured T-shirt, school jumper and unbranded black or navy bottoms. All jewellery must be removed prior to the lesson.
Research shows that children benefit from daily sharing of high-quality stories and poems from a young age: they learn language faster, enter school with a larger vocabulary and become more successful readers (Mol et al., 2008). At Aragon, we value the importance of Early Reading and always ensure every child participates in a daily story session. We want to develop a love of reading both at Nursery and at home. To do this, we have a 'Reading for Pleasure' scheme!
Our Reading for Pleasure scheme enables you and your child to choose a story from our ranging selection of books to take home and share together. Stories provide a great opportunity for discussions about stories and language, and we encourage you to talk about the story with your child afterwards. Talk about the characters, their favourite part of the story, what they can see in the pictures and more!
Every child will be provided with a reading diary where you will be able to record any comments in regard to the stories you share at home, as well as photographs and even encouraging your child to draw pictures relating to the stories they have listened to at home.
Free fruit is provided for the children to have as a healthy snack during the school day. Children must come to school with a water bottle (containing water only, not squash or juice) which can be refilled throughout the school day. Please make sure their water bottle is clearly labelled and placed in the water bottle box outside of the nursery entrance.
We hope that this information is useful in supporting your child at home and please do contact any of the Nursery team should you have any queries.
We encourage children to start nursery potty trained. Whilst accidents are a normal part of learning, being potty trained helps children feel more confident and comfortable throughout the nursery day.
We understand that every child develops at their own pace and we are here to help. If you are starting or continuing potty training at home, please speak to a member of the nursery team. We can work together to provide consistent support and strategies to help your child become confident and independent in using the toilet.
Please ensure your child has a change of clothes in a named bag while they are learning this important skill. We are always happy to discuss any concerns and offer advice and guidance along the way.
We are starting this term with the topic, Magical Me, we are reading Goldilocks and the three bears, Owl Babies and Funny Bones. We will be leaning about each other’s families and drawing portraits. To support this topic, if you would like to, please send in a family photo for our classroom display.
A member of the Nursery Team will be on the door to greet the children daily, please feel free to come and see us with any messages, communication is important, please be mindful of the entrance ramp, and that it is left clear for the children to enter without congestion to ensure a smooth arrival to school and a positive start to their day.
Your child will be encouraged to make their own choices as well as take part in adult-led activities throughout their time in Nursery. Our continuous provision within the environment is set up purposefully to encourage children’s learning and development to take place through their natural curiosity.​ We observe children individually, ensuring that each child is given the opportunity to learn and develop a broad range of skills through play, based on their interests and level of development. ​​
Children will participate in various carpet and small group sessions each day. These sessions will focus on a range of key learning and skills such as fine motor, early reading and writing, maths, topic-based learning and much more!

pageCache.pageTitle: Aragon Primary School - Smartphone Free School
pageCache.text:
Smartphone Free School
At Aragon Primary School, we are committed to providing a safe, focused and inclusive environment in which every child can learn, play and develop positive relationships.
We believe that primary-aged children benefit from real-life social interaction, active play, hands-on experiences and time away from digital distractions. Our Smartphone-Free Policy supports pupils’ wellbeing, emotional development and online safety, while helping us to maintain a strong and connected school community.
We are introducing our smartphone-free approach in stages:
Any permitted phone must be switched off and handed to a member of staff immediately on arrival. It will be stored securely during the school day and returned at home time. Phones must not be used anywhere on the school site, including before or after the school day.
This expectation also applies during school trips, residential visits and other school-led activities.
Smartphones provide access to the internet, social media, messaging applications, cameras and online content. These features can create risks that primary-aged children may not yet have the maturity or experience to manage safely.
Our smartphone-free approach is also about creating a clear and consistent expectation across our school community. We know that parents and carers can sometimes feel under pressure when children ask for a smartphone because they believe that their friends already have one. By making our position clear, families can confidently explain that smartphones are not part of primary school life at Aragon.
We hope this reduces the expectation that primary-aged children should own a smartphone and helps to prevent children from feeling that they need to ask for one. It also supports parents and carers who wish to delay smartphone ownership by giving them a clear school-wide expectation to refer to.
Our approach is intended to:
The policy identifies concerns including cyberbullying, unsuitable content, emotional wellbeing, distraction from learning, privacy risks and social pressure.
We recommend delaying the purchase of a smartphone for as long as possible.
Where families feel that their child needs a phone for travelling independently, we recommend choosing a basic mobile phone.
A basic mobile phone is designed primarily for:
Unlike a smartphone, a basic mobile phone does not provide access to social media, applications or internet browsing.
When purchasing a phone or SIM card, we recommend:
The examples included in our policy are provided to help families understand the types of basic mobile phones available. They are not endorsements of particular products or retailers.
Smartwatches, GPS watches, Bluetooth tags and other location-tracking devices must not be brought into school, worn during the school day or taken on school trips.
These devices may transmit location information through external applications or cloud services that are outside the school’s control. Tracking information can also be delayed or inaccurate and may interfere with the school’s established safeguarding procedures, including registers, headcounts and emergency responses.
We recognise that, in exceptional circumstances, a child may require a smartphone to operate an essential medical application, such as a glucose-monitoring system.
Where this applies, parents and carers should contact the school office so that an appropriate individual arrangement can be agreed with the Headteacher. Any approved device will be used only for its medical purpose and managed securely throughout the school day.
Any unauthorised smartphone, smart tracker or internet-enabled device will be confiscated and stored securely. The school office will contact the child’s parent or carer, and the device must be collected by a family adult.
Permitted basic mobile phones must also be handed in on arrival. Where a phone is not handed in, it may be confiscated and returned directly to a parent or carer. Repeated breaches may result in further action in line with the school’s Behaviour Policy.
We strongly recommend delaying smartphone ownership for as long as possible and choosing a basic mobile phone where a child needs to contact their family.
However, we recognise that some parents and carers may decide to allow their child to use a smartphone outside school. Where this is the case, we strongly recommend setting up parental controls before giving the device to your child.
Please remember that smartphones must not be brought onto the school site, even when parental controls have been enabled.
Apple’s Family Sharing and Screen Time settings allow parents and carers to manage a child’s device. These controls can be used to:
We recommend creating a separate child Apple Account through Family Sharing and protecting the Screen Time settings with a passcode that is not shared with your child. Apple provides step-by-step guidance for setting up and managing these controls.
Google’s Family Link service allows parents and carers to supervise a child’s Google Account and compatible Android device. It can be used to:
Parents and carers can install the Family Link app on their own Android phone, iPhone or iPad and connect it to the child’s supervised Google Account.
Internet Matters provides clear, step-by-step guides for setting up parental controls on Apple and Android devices. It also offers guidance on making a smartphone more limited by removing or restricting internet browsing, social media, applications and downloads.
Parental controls are an important safeguard, but they cannot remove every online risk. We also encourage families to:
encourage face-to-face conversation, friendship and active play;
support healthy emotional regulation and independence;
protect children’s personal information and privacy;
making and receiving telephone calls;
